title: Second distinction: honor propter se vs propter aliud—rational nature vs sacred signs
source_text: XXXVII. Secundo dicunt posse aliquid honorari propter se, vel propter aliud. Id honoratur, inquiunt, propter se, quod habet in se rationem venerationis non dependentem aliunde; & hoc modo sola natura rationalis est venerabilis. Propter aliud honoratur id, quod habet in se quidem causam honoris, sed illa causa tota pendet ab alio. Et hoc modo signa rerum sacrarum sunt venerabilia: habent enim in se relationem similitudinis, sive repraesentationem rei sacrae, & proinde quandam excellentiam, sed illa tota pendet ab ipsa re sacra.
pass_a_gloss: Secondly they say that something can be honored on account of itself, or on account of another. That is honored on account of itself, they say, which has in itself a reason of veneration not depending from elsewhere; and in this way rational nature alone is venerable. On account of another is honored that which has in itself indeed a cause of honor, but that cause wholly depends on another. And in this way the signs of sacred things are venerable: for they have in themselves a relation of likeness, or a representation of a sacred thing, and accordingly a certain excellence, but that wholly depends on the sacred thing itself.
pass_b_english: Second cut: honor on account of itself vs on account of another.
Only rational nature is venerable propter se; sacred signs are venerable only propter aliud, because their excellence hangs entirely on the holy thing they represent.

lemmas.gloss: on account of itself, or on account of another

choices.why: Alone venerable propter se in this School frame.
